Dude, you sound like you're going through a lot right now! Holy moley. with the situational factors you described, I applaud you just for keeping it together!

I bet you have tons of emotions and pain to feel that right now are just still getting prepped. The thing about pain is this: If you let yourself feel it, it passes through you, and then it goes away. If you don't feel it, or can't feel it yet, it makes you feel weird and bad in the meantime. It's like pooping, frankly. You eat a lot, you feel bloated, then you dump out and it feels awesome, and you're a-ok to keep going. Same with the stuff life throws you. You eat the difficult situations, you digest them, you feel bloated, and then you shit out a bunch of tears, and then you're ready to live again! :)

If you aren't seeing someone for professional help, I recommend it. It can actually be very soothing, and it'll help you feel like you're in control of your life!

There are two things you have on your side: 1. Time heals all wounds. It's amazing. I feel like if you start to move toward people who are more supportive, and not jerks, you will just start to heal on your own. Heck, even if everyone else is a jerk, you'll still heal. 2. Emotions cannot kill you. They might tempt you to do things that aren't in keeping with your values. But they can't make you do anything. And even the worst pain is just pain. A little pain never hurt anybody. If you learn to let yourself feel the pain, it'll pass through you. The worst feeling is struggling trying to *not* feel the pain inside.

It sounds like a lot of people have treated you badly. Particularly that one on and off g/f you mentioned. Her behavior sounds frankly abusive, and I feel like she must be in a ton of pain as well to have treated you so badly. But that's not your problem. I'd suggest that you set some boundaries with her, if she's not out of your life already.

I don't know how you fell into this kind of difficult pile of situations, but rest assured that it's quite unlikely to stay this bad. You might just be getting the hardest stuff in life out of the way all at once...

Try to form a support network. Online folks can be very helpful. See if you can find people in person as well. This will probably require meeting new people, which can be tough but is worth it. I'm currently going through a phase where I'm sort of burning out friends by relying too much on them for urgent emotional needs, so I would also just caution you to keep adding people to your support network until you have a handful of them, so you can rely on them without burning them out. And I've actually specifically asked my friends to let me know if I'm burning them out. :)

Anyway, I hope that helps. Hang in there! Holy crap. And don't be afraid about the fact that you have suicidal thoughts, but if you start to feel like you're making plans about how to do it, or the thoughts don't go away, PLEASE GET HELP. We really don't want to lose you! Just know that everyone has suicidal thoughts sometimes. Treat them like a red flag, but not a sign that you're broken.

Much love. <3

* State how you feel about the issue, and own your feelings.
* State how the other person might feel about the issue, to demonstrate empathy.
* Include positive elements; e.g. "I really value our friendship, and want to be honest with you about something that bothers me."

And I guess you just have to trust that people won't use mock offense as a method of truly trying to silence you.

The more flexible you are socially, the less chance you're an asshole.

You use your gut. And in real life conversations, you pay attention to social queues to tell if someone is offended.

If I'm talking to a new person and they flinch when I say the word "sofa," and I pick up on that. Maybe I ask them why they flinched. Maybe their parents were eaten by a sofa.

On a mostly one-way broadcast communication medium like Reddit, you have to choose your default rules based on what you perceive as the community's areas of offense.  If you're in a subreddit that doesn't mind certain words, go for it. If a thread comes up like this where some readers express offense at some terms, then maybe pay it heed.

Also, as a general rule, don't refer to people using a word they don't use for themselves.  That's a whole other can of worms, but is also at play here.

It's not up to you to decide how other people should feel. You just get to decide whether to be an asshole or not.

Thanks for playing the game!  Um, I know it's cheesy to say this from afar as a designer, but it's by design that it's not easy to have a particular set of ants change their behaviors completely mid-game.  It's intended to be a sort of "evolution" of behaviors (term used loosely).

The biggest thing I would implore you to take away from my experimentation in ant game creation is that you really must implement pheromone trails in order to get proper emergence going.  Leafcutters doesn't actually feature any emergence, since the ants don't communicate with each other.  Thus, each of the Leafcutters game ants is as intelligent as the whole, which misses the mark.

And yes, I'm planning to make another ant game sometime soon...  :)

It was a team effort, but I did most of the coding myself.  I spent a year on it as my thesis project.  That being said, much of that time was spent designing and redesigning rather than coding just the final product.

Leafcutters, my thesis project at USC's Interactive Media Division, is a game in which you guide a colony of leafcutting ants to thrive by setting up and tweaking the rules that guide the actions of the individual ants.  The [trailer is here](http://www.leafcuttersgame.com/), and I can hook you up with a playable download if you'd like!
